questions.q_en: Which of the following observations was made by Hans Christian Oersted in 1820?
options_en: Moving charges do not produce a magnetic field.
A current in a straight wire causes a noticeable deflection in a nearby magnetic compass needle.
Electricity and magnetism are unrelated phenomena.
Light is not an electromagnetic wave.
questions.solution_en:
· In 1820, Hans Christian Oersted noticed during a lecture demonstration that a current in a straight wire caused a noticeable deflection in a nearby magnetic compass needle.

· He investigated this phenomenon and concluded that moving charges or currents produced a magnetic field.

· The realization that electricity and magnetism were intimately related stemmed from this discovery.

· The understanding of light as an electromagnetic wave came later with Maxwell.

questions.q_en: The magnetic field lines of a bar magnet (or a solenoid) have which of the following characteristics?
options_en: They originate from the north pole and end at the south pole outside the magnet and do not form closed loops.
The tangent to the field line at a given point does not represent the direction of the net magnetic field B at that point.
questions.solution_en:
· The magnetic field lines of a magnet (or a solenoid) form continuous closed loops.

· Unlike electric field lines, they do not begin and end on charges.

· The tangent to the field line at a given point represents the direction of the net magnetic field B at that point, and magnetic field lines do not intersect because the direction of the magnetic field would not be unique at the point of intersection.

questions.q_en: The Biot-Savart law is used to determine the magnetic field due to which of the following?
options_en: A permanent magnet at a large distance.
questions.solution_en:
The Biot-Savart law specifically relates to the magnetic field generated by an electric current.

It states that the magnetic field dB at a point due to a current element I dl is given by:

dB = (μ₀/4π) X (I dl X r̂)/r²

This law applies to a current-carrying element.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the magnetic properties of materials?

I. Diamagnetic substances have a small positive magnetic susceptibility.

II. Paramagnetic substances have a small negative magnetic susceptibility.

III. Ferromagnetic substances can retain magnetisation even after the external field is removed.
questions.solution_en:
Diamagnetic substances have a small positive magnetic susceptibility. This is incorrect. Diamagnetic substances have a small negative magnetic susceptibility (χ < 0).

When placed in an external magnetic field, they develop a weak magnetization in the opposite direction to the applied field, resulting in a repulsive effect.

Paramagnetic substances have a small negative magnetic susceptibility. This is incorrect. Paramagnetic substances have a small positive magnetic susceptibility (χ > 0).

When placed in an external magnetic field, they develop a weak magnetization in the same direction as the applied field, resulting in a weak attractive effect.

Ferromagnetic substances can retain magnetisation even after the external field is removed. This is correct.

Ferromagnetic materials (such as iron, cobalt, and nickel) can retain their magnetization even after the external magnetic field is removed.

This property is called remanence or magnetic hysteresis and is the basis for permanent magnets.

questions.q_en: The force on a straight conductor of length l carrying a steady current I in a uniform external magnetic field B is given by:
questions.solution_en:
The force on a straight conductor of length l and carrying a steady current I in a uniform external magnetic field B is given by F = I l X B, where the direction of l is given by the direction of the current.

This is derived from the Lorentz force acting on the moving charge carriers in the wire.

questions.q_en: The magnetic force on a moving charged particle in a magnetic field is:
options_en: always parallel to the magnetic field.
always in the direction of motion of the particle.
perpendicular to both the velocity of the particle and the magnetic field.
independent of the velocity of the particle.
questions.solution_en:
The magnetic force on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field is given by the Lorentz force equation:

F = q(v X B), where F is the force vector, q is the charge of the particle, v is the velocity vector, and B is the magnetic field vector.

According to the properties of the cross product, the resulting force is perpendicular to both the velocity of the particle and the magnetic field.

questions.q_en: Gauss's law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is:
options_en: proportional to the net magnetic pole enclosed.
proportional to the current passing through the surface.
questions.solution_en:
Gauss's law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, mathematically expressed as ∮ B.dS = 0.

This law reflects the fact that isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) are not known to exist.

questions.q_en: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid carrying a current I and having n turns per unit length is given by:
questions.solution_en:
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform and parallel to the axis of the solenoid. Its magnitude is given by the formula: B = μ₀nI

Where:

· B is the magnetic field strength

· μ₀ is the permeability of free space (4π X 10⁻⁷ H/m)

· n is the number of turns per unit length of the solenoid

· I is the current flowing through the solenoid

questions.q_en: According to Ampere's Law, the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop is proportional to:
options_en: The electric field inside the loop
The electric current passing through the area enclosed by the loop
The magnetic flux through the loop
The electric flux through the loop
questions.solution_en:
Ampere's Law states that ∮B·dl = μ₀I, where B is the magnetic field, dl is an infinitesimal segment of the closed loop, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, and I is the total electric current passing through the area enclosed by the loop.

This means the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop is directly proportional to the current enclosed by the loop,

Further information:

· Ampere's Law relates the enclosed current to the magnetic field around a closed loop.

· Lorentz Force describes the force on a moving charge due to electric and magnetic fields.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement(s) accurately describe(s) magnetic field lines?

I. The magnetic field lines of a magnet form continuous closed loops.

II. The tangent to the field line at a point gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point.
questions.solution_en:
Statement I is correct: Magnetic field lines always form continuous closed loops, emerging from the north pole of a magnet and entering the south pole, and continuing through the magnet back to the north pole.

Statement II is correct: At any point on a magnetic field line, the tangent to the line represents the direction of the magnetic field at that point.

questions.q_en: Which of the following materials exhibits strong magnetization when placed in an external magnetic field and tends to move from a region of weak magnetic field to a strong magnetic field?
questions.solution_en:
Ferromagnetic substances (like iron, cobalt, and nickel) exhibit strong magnetization in the presence of an external magnetic field. They have a high magnetic permeability and tend to move from a region of weaker magnetic field to a region of stronger magnetic field due to their strong alignment of magnetic domains.

· Diamagnetic substances are repelled by magnetic fields and move from strong to weak field regions.

· Paramagnetic substances are weakly attracted to magnetic fields but show only slight magnetization.

· Ferromagnetic substances are the only ones with strong magnetization.

questions.q_en: The force between two parallel current-carrying conductors is a consequence of:
options_en: electrostatic forces between the moving charges.
the magnetic field produced by one conductor exerting a force on the moving charges in the other conductor.
the electric field produced by one conductor affecting the current in the other.
questions.solution_en:
When a current flows through a conductor, it creates a magnetic field around it.

If there are two parallel current-carrying conductors, the magnetic field created by one conductor interacts with the moving charges (current) in the other, resulting in a magnetic force between the two.

This is the basis of the definition of the ampere.

questions.q_en: The torque τ on a current loop with magnetic moment m placed in a uniform magnetic field B is given by:
questions.solution_en:
The torque on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field B is given by the vector product of the magnetic moment m of the coil and the magnetic field: τ = m X B.

The magnitude of the torque is τ = m B sin θ, where θ is the angle between m and B.

questions.q_en: What happens to a diamagnetic substance when placed in an external magnetic field?
options_en: It gets strongly magnetized in the direction of the field.
It gets weakly magnetized in the direction of the field.
It is repelled by the field and the field inside is reduced.
It has no interaction with the magnetic field.
questions.solution_en:
Diamagnetic substances are repelled by magnetic fields. When placed in an external magnetic field, they develop a weak magnetic moment in the opposite direction to the applied field. As a result, the magnetic field inside the diamagnetic material is reduced.

This repulsive behavior is a defining characteristic of diamagnetism and occurs in all materials, but is usually only noticeable in substances like bismuth or superconductors, which show strong diamagnetic effects.

questions.q_en: What is the path of a charged particle moving with a velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B?
questions.solution_en:
When a charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity perpendicular to the field, it experiences a magnetic force that acts as a centripetal force, constantly pulling the particle toward the center of a circular path.

This results in the particle moving in a circular orbit, with the magnetic force perpendicular to its velocity at all times, changing the direction but not the magnitude of the velocity.

questions.q_en: When a bar magnet is broken into two pieces:
options_en: One piece becomes a north pole and the other becomes a south pole
Each piece becomes a separate magnet with its own north and south poles
The magnetism is concentrated in one piece while the other becomes non-magnetic
questions.solution_en:
A bar magnet consists of aligned magnetic domains, and every atom acts like a tiny magnet. When you break a bar magnet into two pieces, each piece still has these aligned domains.

As a result, each piece becomes a smaller magnet with both a north and a south pole. No matter how many times you cut a magnet, you'll always get smaller magnets with two poles.
